title: Band reaction; not louder but another colour behind the brass
summary: Younger and some older musicians liked the lift; Clarke says he played not louder but as a springboard behind the brass.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, did you -- when you started playing like this, did the whole brass section -- did everybody dig it?
Yes. The younger guys. And some of the older guys, they felt that because it kind of made what they were doing much more emphatic, you know?
Because they heard these things behind them and it gave such a lift to the band, you know?
But one thing it meant, I think -- I don't know -- but it meant that the drums had to be louder, because if they were -- in a sense, didn't it?
No, not louder, but sort of --
Another tone behind it, behind the brass, another color behind the brass.
Yeah. But would you say that it was an introduction to drumming that was louder? That it opened the field up for drumming that did become louder?
Yeah, that's more about the size of it, you know.
Because I would try not to play too loud, not to drown out the brass.
But to kind of give them the backing.
That I felt they needed. You know, by playing different passages with them, and then playing sort of like passages before we -- I mean to bring them into this passage.
Because I knew exactly where they were going.
So I could kind of give them the right springboard they needed.
Well, you gave them a concept, a whole concept that was different, was new.
